_README: Subject matter expert sign-off. See review_ledger.py for the mechanism.
This list is EMPTY because nothing has been reviewed. That is the honest
state, not an oversight. 347 authored facts and 83 misconceptions are
cited but unverified, and the platform says so on the compliance report
and in the UI rather than implying otherwise.
Do not add an entry here on anyone's behalf. A row in this file asserts
that a named person with the standing to judge it checked a specific
claim against the work it cites. Writing one without that having happened
is fabricating an expert review, which is worse than having none, because
it converts an honest gap into a false assurance.
To add a real one:
1. GET /api/v1/review-queue.csv, or call export_csv(), and
send the reviewer the rows for their area.
2. They fill in verdict, reviewer and note. item_id must come back
unchanged; it is what binds a row to its claim.
3. Commit the rows here, in a PR that names them. The commit IS the
sign-off, which is why this is a file and not an endpoint.
verdict is 'confirmed' or 'disputed'. There is no 'corrected': fixing a
claim changes its wording, which changes its item_id, which returns it to
pending for a fresh look. A review is bound to the exact text it was
given, so any edit costs the sign-off and the orphaned entry is reported
as stale and blocks the compliance run.
reviewer should identify the person and their standing well enough that
someone could go back and ask them, e.g. 'Dr A. Rivera, Associate
Professor of Organic Chemistry, University of X'. A bare first name is
rejected by the loader.
